correctness.rationale: For order at least seven, every pair has a third vertex adjacent to neither; all six one-round pair extension classes follow exhaustively from degree two. The resulting three two-round vertex types and their rank-three set classify all large graphs. Rank-three formulas distinguish the three bits, and a dominating-pair sentence separates the five small cases; the small cases are pairwise distinguished by triangles, nonadjacent twins, and existence of a common neighbor for every nonedge. Explicit representatives and a 3+4+5 vertex lower bound prove the sharp order 12. Recursive type computation and an independent adversarial game solver reproduce the finite checks. No unproved finite-to-infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: Natural complete rank-three classification of all finite 2-regular graphs (including arbitrary connected-component multiplicities), not a single-parameter renaming. The new disjoint-union behavior is structurally nontrivial: two C_5 components become equivalent to a long connected cycle although one C_5 does not. Twelve exact classes, a three-bit invariant above six vertices, explicit minimal representatives, and a sharp 12-vertex finite-model cutoff aid test cases and logic expressivity comparisons. General results on bounded-degree locality do not directly yield these sharp constants.
